subject: English
title: CISCE curriculum: English, Class I

source.read: A third-party copy of the Class I pages of the CISCE curriculum (English: printed pages 6 to 9), hosted by BYJU'S
source.note: UNOFFICIAL SOURCE. The pages do not name their publisher or year, and were read through a text summary of the PDF, not the PDF itself. The official document on cisce.org could not be reached from the build environment. CISCE is understood not to prescribe a textbook for this class, so a school's own book and term plan may order or extend these topics.

licence: Strand names as printed (facts). Every outcome is written by OpenPath in its own words with a pointer to its strand and line; no curriculum text is reproduced.
review: OpenPath curriculum inventory (research from a secondary source; not an educator review)

outcomes.text: Follows the ways of the class: listens to others and takes turns.
outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Keeps a conversation going by answering what others say.
outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Says simple poems with fitting actions.
outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Understands a text read aloud by answering and asking about its key details.
outcomes.note: Answering questions on a passage heard is practised; asking them is not.

outcomes.text: Answers simple questions about stories.
Asks questions to clear up doubts.
outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Describes people, places and things.

outcomes.text: Uses words and phrases picked up from talk and from texts.
outcomes.note: First words teaches everyday words by ear; using them in speech is not heard by the app.

outcomes.text: Gives full sentences that suit the task.
outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Gives and follows simple two-step directions.
outcomes.note: Following a two-step direction (tap this, then that) is practised in First words; giving directions aloud is not heard by the app.

outcomes.text: Reads with the help of pictures.
Reads alone and in a group, with understanding.
outcomes.note: The first reading level has short texts with questions; reading in a group is not in the app.

outcomes.text: Adds drawings to make ideas and feelings clear.
outcomes.note: Done with a grown-up, away from the app, who ticks what they saw.

outcomes.text: Says who is telling the story at different points.
outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Reads a text of the class level smoothly, pausing in the right places.
outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Writes words and sentences in clear print letters.
outcomes.note: Done with a grown-up, away from the app, who ticks what they saw.

outcomes.text: Starts a sentence with a capital letter and ends it with a full stop.
Draws and writes about familiar topics.
outcomes.note: Written here or on paper to a task set for this class. The learner checks it against a short list and a grown-up ticks what they see. The app does not keep or mark the writing; the essay studio gives a closer analysis where an evaluator is connected.

outcomes.text: Tells events in order with the help of pictures, and says how people reacted.
Answers classmates' questions and adds details to improve a piece of writing.
outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Recalls or gathers information to answer a question.
outcomes.note: Done with a grown-up, away from the app, who ticks what they saw.

outcomes.text: Takes dictation of three- and four-letter words and short sentences.
Writes eight to ten sentences on a topic.
outcomes.note: Written here or on paper to a task set for this class. The learner checks it against a short list and a grown-up ticks what they see. The app does not keep or mark the writing; the essay studio gives a closer analysis where an evaluator is connected.

outcomes.text: Uses naming, action, describing and position words, and opposites.
outcomes.note: Naming, action, describing and position words are practised in First words. Opposites are met there as pairs (hot and cold, happy and sad) and by name in Grammar in use.

outcomes.text: Knows one and many, and he and she.
Uses a, an and the correctly.
Writes every capital and small letter.
outcomes.note: Done with a grown-up, away from the app, who ticks what they saw.

outcomes.text: Uses common, proper and possessive nouns.
Matches nouns for one and for many with the right verbs.
Uses verbs for the simple past, present and future.
Uses common adjectives, joining words, determiners and prepositions.
Gives proper nouns a capital letter.
Uses commas, full stops, question marks and exclamation marks.
Spells words not yet taught by their sounds.
outcomes.note: The Spelling Bee dictates words and teaches the rule after a mistake; sounding out a new word is not taught as such.

outcomes.text: Puts words in alphabetical order by their first letter.
Uses words suited to the age.
Spells three- and four-letter words.
